messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected on dedicated-pool-eu1 for model: redwood/turbo-alpha. p95=820ms, p99=2.5s over last 3m; streaming stalls observed. Autoscaler did not add capacity within expected handshake window (observed delay ~45s). Queue depth spiked to 650. Affected: a small subset of Dedicated customers (tenant tags: enterprise-*, reserved-capacity). Paging on-call.
jordan.m (oncall): ack. I’m on it — collecting quick context. Is there a recent deploy or config change? Any scheduled maintenance on eu1?
lee.r (eng-runtime): not aware of a deploy. Telemetry: warmup success rate dropped ~60% for cold pools, KV cache misses spiked. Handshake latencies to provisioned workers show timeouts at the pool manager side. Looks like a simultaneous burst from multiple tenants hitting reserved pools.
priya.s (support): customers CUST-314 and CUST-922 reported intermittent streaming stalls and partial responses. Support is triaging with customers; asking for ETA and mitigation steps we can relay.
sam.k (eng-platform): adding more logs — here's the tail from the autoscaler controller for the period:

```
2026-03-15T12:03:14Z controller: request received tenant=CUST-314 burst=high
2026-03-15T12:03:15Z controller: attempted handshake pool=dedicated-pool-eu1 nodes_needed=4
2026-03-15T12:03:18Z runtime: warmup started for node n-304
2026-03-15T12:04:00Z controller: handshake timeout waiting for heartbeat from n-304
2026-03-15T12:04:10Z controller: fallback policy not engaged; autoscale delay total=46s
2026-03-15T12:04:20Z metrics: queue_depth=650 p99=2.3s
```

sam.k (eng-platform): CLI snapshot of current capacity:

```
redwoodctl pools describe dedicated-pool-eu1 --json
"desired": 12,
"ready": 8,
"pending_warmup": 5
```

jordan.m (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) manually scale up to reduce queue (if possible), 2) enable emergency fallback routing to smaller quantized model for streaming, 3) temp increase priority for enterprise tenants. I’ll kick off manual scale and coordinate with eng-runtime for fallback.
ops-rotations: note - see runbook step: Dedicated pool warmup handoff -> manual_scale_then_reroute. Paging SREs in the runbook channel.
lee.r (eng-runtime): I can enable fallback routing. Suggest map requests for enterprise-* to redwood/turbo-alpha-quant (lower mem footprint) and enable KV cache prefetch for active tenants. Doing a controlled traffic split 80/20 to fallback.
lee.r (eng-runtime): executing traffic split now. Command:

```
redwoodctl routing split --pool dedicated-pool-eu1 --from=redwood/turbo-alpha --to=redwood/turbo-alpha-quant --percent=20 --tag-filter=\"tenant:enterprise-*\"
```

lee.r (eng-runtime): fallback routing applied :white_check_mark:
jordan.m (oncall): starting manual scale: increasing desired nodes by 6 to match pending warmup. Command:

```
redwoodctl pools scale dedicated-pool-eu1 --delta 6
```

jordan.m (oncall): executed. Watching warmup.
sam.k (eng-platform): noticed autoscaler controller backlog — controller queue worker crashed once during burst (OOM in handshake manager). Restarted the controller process; crash dump attached to internal link. Restart should allow autoscaler to resume normal behaviour.
lee.r (eng-runtime): enabling KV cache prefetch for CUST-314 and CUST-922 to reduce cold path hits.
lee.r (eng-runtime): prefetch command:

```
redwoodctl kv prefetch --tenants CUST-314,CUST-922 --model redwood/turbo-alpha
```

priya.s (support): update for customers: telling them we’ve enabled a fallback model and scaled the pool; asking to monitor. Will update CUST-314 via private channel. Any ETA on when p99 will return to SLO?
jordan.m (oncall): warmup progress: 3/6 new nodes warmed in 90s. Queue depth decreasing from 650 -> 210.
ops-rotations: marking incident as LIVEPAGE in PagerDuty for 15m to monitor after mitigations.
lee.r (eng-runtime): after routing + prefetch, we saw p95 -> 240ms, p99 -> 680ms within 2 minutes. Streaming stalls reduced. :thumbsup:
sam.k (eng-platform): controller is stable, pending warmup now 2, ready 14, desired 18. CLI:

```
"desired": 18,
"ready": 14,
"pending_warmup": 2
```

jordan.m (oncall): p99 dropped below SLO threshold (now 560ms). Reducing emergency routing to 5% to test rollback.
lee.r (eng-runtime): reduced fallback split to 5% — command run. Monitoring for regressions.
priya.s (support): CUST-314 confirmed degraded UX improved; CUST-922 waiting on logfile correlation but no further stalls reported.
ops-rotations: quick post-incident notes: probable root cause = simultaneous reserved-tenant bursts + autoscaler controller instability (OOM during handshake) causing delayed warmup. Action items: 1) investigate controller OOM and add backpressure guard, 2) improve handshake timeouts and fallbacks in autoscaler, 3) implement per-tenant burst smoothing (rate limit bursts at pool ingress), 4) runbook update for faster manual scale steps.
sam.k (eng-platform): created ticket PLAT-2092 for controller OOM + guard and linked crash dump.
lee.r (eng-runtime): created ticket RUNTIME-1137 to add faster fallback policy and pre-warm hooks for reserved tenants.
jordan.m (oncall): setting a 2-hour postmortem sync with oncall + eng-runtime + platform + support. I’ll own initial writeup. Anyone else want to co-author? priya.s (support) volunteered to add customer-impact section.
priya.s (support): happy to co-author. I’ll add transcript of customer messages and timestamps.
ops-rotations: marking thread resolved when metrics remain stable for 30m. Leaving the page open for monitoring. :eyes:
lee.r (eng-runtime): note for follow-up — consider adding proactive warmup for tenants with scheduled high traffic (webhooks/jobs) to avoid sudden cold starts.
jordan.m (oncall): thanks all. Immediate status: mitigations applied, p99 back under SLO, manual scale completed. Leaving monitoring for 30m. Will file postmortem and link here. :white_check_mark:
